history.text:
Who this is for: a freelancer or small studio invoicing other businesses for services.

Default: Net 30, credit limit equal to the invoice, when the client is active, has traded for 3+ years, has filed recent accounts and has no gazette or court trouble.

Ask a 30% deposit when any of these is true: the company is under 2 years old; its latest accounts are 6+ months overdue; a commercial court ruled against it in the last 12 months; the invoice is above 10,000 EUR and nothing is known about its finances.

Ask a 50% deposit when: its accounts are 18+ months overdue or were never filed; or its last filed year shows a loss above 20% of revenue, or negative equity.

Prepay only when: a past insolvency proceeding ended less than 3 years ago under a continuation plan; or two or more deposit triggers fire together.

Decline when: the company is in liquidation, has ceased trading, or is sanctioned.

Conflicting signals: the most recent dated fact wins, and a hard fact (gazette, court, filing date) beats a soft one. Never offer more than 45 days.
warnings: For a client whose accounts are 24 months overdue, the policy gives a 50% deposit, but the program gives prepay (rules deposit_30_accounts_6_plus_months_overdue, deposit_50_accounts_18_plus_months_overdue, prepay_two_or_more_deposit_triggers fire). Fix the rules so they agree with the policy.
For a healthy client with a €40,000 invoice, the policy gives a 30% deposit, but the program gives Net 30 (no rule fires). Fix the rules so they agree with the policy.

history.rationale: I tightened the 30% and 50% deposit thresholds around the late-filing and overdue patterns that were most often missed, while narrowing prepay to the combinations that showed stronger failure evidence and avoiding the false-alarm cases.
warnings: For a healthy client whose accounts are 9 months overdue, the policy gives a 30% deposit, but the program gives a 50% deposit (rules deposit_50_accounts_6plus_months_overdue fire). Fix the rules so they agree with the policy.
For a healthy client with a €40,000 invoice, the policy gives a 30% deposit, but the program gives Net 30 (rules net_30_clean_client fire). Fix the rules so they agree with the policy.

history.text:
Who this is for: a freelancer or small studio invoicing other businesses for services.

Default: Net 30, credit limit equal to the invoice, when the client is active, has traded for 3+ years, has filed recent accounts and has no gazette or court trouble.

Ask a 30% deposit when any of these is true: the company is under 2 years old; its latest accounts are 6+ months overdue; a commercial court ruled against it in the last 12 months; the invoice is above 10,000 EUR and nothing is known about its finances; or it has 1-5 months overdue accounts and its last filed accounts were 6+ months late.

Ask a 50% deposit when: its accounts are 18+ months overdue or were never filed; or its last filed year shows a loss above 20% of revenue; or it has 6+ months overdue accounts and its last filed accounts were 1-5 months late.

Prepay only when: a past insolvency proceeding ended less than 3 years ago under a continuation plan; or two or more deposit triggers fire together.

Decline when: the company is in liquidation, has ceased trading, or is sanctioned.

Conflicting signals: the most recent dated fact wins, and a hard fact (gazette, court, filing date) beats a soft one. Never offer more than 45 days.
history.rationale: I tightened the deposit and prepay thresholds using the strongest warning patterns in the mistakes, especially overdue + late-filing combinations, while keeping the decline rules unchanged.

review.reason: The proposed policy is accepted for review with a score of 85, but evaluators had low confidence due to disagreement on correctness (56/100) - some felt the evidence didn't fully support the new deposit thresholds. The strongest evaluator (Cinder) approved it as an economically sound improvement.
